entries.appliesTo: frontier developers of frontier models (>10^26 operations); heavier duties on large frontier developers (> $500,000,000 annual gross revenues)

dutySources.risk-program: § 10(a) — 'a large frontier developer shall write, implement, comply with, and clearly and conspicuously publish on its website a frontier AI framework'
dutySources.documentation: § 10(c)(1) — 'Before, or concurrently with, deploying a new frontier model or a substantially modified version of an existing frontier model, a frontier developer shall clearly and conspicuously publish on its website a transparency report'
dutySources.impact-assessment: § 10(e) — 'A large frontier developer shall transmit to the Agency a summary of any assessment of catastrophic risk resulting from internal use of its frontier models every 3 months'
dutySources.incident-reporting: § 15(c) — 'A frontier developer shall report any critical safety incident pertaining to one or more of its frontier models to the Agency and the Attorney General within 72 hours'
dutySources.registration-filing: § 18(a) — 'no large frontier developer may develop, deploy, or operate a frontier model, in whole or in part in this State, without having a current disclosure statement filed with the Agency and paying the required fee'

exposure.enforcer: attorney-general (exclusive civil action); Agency levies registration penalties

sources.threshold: § 5 — '"Frontier model" means a foundation model that was trained using a quantity of computing power greater than 10 26 integer or floating-point operations' (superscript 10^26 flattened in text extraction)
sources.safetyFramework: § 10(a) — 'shall write, implement, comply with, and clearly and conspicuously publish on its website a frontier AI framework'
sources.incidentReporting: § 15(c) — 'shall report any critical safety incident pertaining to one or more of its frontier models to the Agency and the Attorney General within 72 hours'
sources.thirdPartyAudit: § 10(d) — 'a large frontier developer shall annually retain a third party to perform an independent audit of compliance with the requirements of this Section'
sources.whistleblower: § 20(a) — 'A frontier developer shall not make, adopt, enforce, or enter into a rule, regulation, policy, or contract that prevents a covered employee from disclosing, or retaliates against a covered employee for disclosing'
sources.penaltyMax: § 25(a) — 'For a subsequent violation, the civil penalty may not exceed $3,000,000 per violation.'
sources.enforcer: § 25(b) — 'recovered in a civil action brought exclusively by the Attorney General'; § 18(e) — 'the Agency may, after notice and hearing, levy civil penalties, fees, and costs'

flags: first-violation penalty capped lower: § 25(a) — 'does not exceed $1,000,000 for the first violation'; coded penaltyMax is the subsequent-violation cap
separate registration penalty: § 18(e)(1) — 'a civil penalty of $1,000 for each day the person fails to file a disclosure as required by this Section or fails to correct false information'

dual applicability threshold: compute (10^26 ops defines frontier model) plus revenue tier — § 5: 'Large frontier developer' means one with 'annual gross revenues in excess of $500,000,000 in the preceding calendar year'; threshold param coded as compute, revenue tier is lossy

most duties bind only large frontier developers; the § 10(c)(1) transparency report, § 15(c) incident reporting, § 10(f) no-false-statements rule, and § 20 whistleblower protections bind all frontier developers
annual third-party compliance audit (§ 10(d)) fits no listed duty key; captured via thirdPartyAudit param only
whistleblower notice-posting (§ 20(d)) and anonymous internal disclosure process with monthly updates (§ 20(e)) fit no listed duty key
interoperability safe harbor: § 17(b)(2)(A) — compliance with a designated federal law/regulation/guidance is 'deemed in compliance with this Act' after declaring intent to the Agency
annual pro rata fee assessment on large frontier developers for administration costs (§ 18(d))

no private right of action: § 25(d); state preemption of home rule: § 35; Sections 80 and 90 are conforming amendments (FOIA exemption, Whistleblower Act) supporting the same regime, not separate segments
effective January 1, 2027 (§ 99); frontier AI framework and audit duties begin January 1, 2028 (§ 10(a), (d))
